content.text:
I built `spec.vl.json` and checked it with `render`: it renders with no errors or warnings. The answer to the question is mostly yes: most years run high in winter and low in summer. Early 2021 had no winter wave, and 2022 rose unusually early and peaked in December.

The heatmap has one row per ISO year (2012–2026) and one column per ISO week (1–53). The data is loaded straight from the URL, and all filtering and parsing happens inside the spec.

```
REPORT
deliverable: spec.vl.json
requirements:
  R1: done - ordinal y on ISO year from Kalenderwoche, ascending top to bottom (2012–2026)
  R2: done - ordinal x on ISO week 1–53; week 53 cells appear only in 2015 and 2020
  R3: done - sequential yelloworangered scale; legend "ARE consultations per 100,000 per week"
  R4: done - only reported weeks are drawn; 2012 before W40 and 2026 after W43 are blank
  R5: done - week numbers on the top x axis, years on the y axis
  R6: done - title plus a one-sentence caption as the subtitle
assumptions:
  - ISO year and week are taken from the Kalenderwoche string (YYYY-Www), not from Saison
  - The week axis is placed at the top so labels sit next to the first rows
  - The caption text is my reading of the rendered figure; it is not computed from the data
limitations:
  - Weeks are columns of equal width, so they show no calendar-date detail
  - The caption describes the data as of commit 65ac2d2 and would need rewording if the data changed
```
